names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Οκτωβρίου, «Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής και Πατρίκιος», with the rank word left off.
The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 1614, «Никита Константинопольский, Исповедник, прп.», with the rank words left off. The day line gives «Никиты исп» alone.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 октября ст. ст. — «Прп. Никиты исп (ок. 838).»
source.note: No rank is read onto this line. The day prints two icons and both stand in its first paragraph — a polyeleos before the Iveron icon of the Theotokos, and the plain service, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all, before the company of 251 — and neither reaches a later line. The one further polyeleos the day's readings name is Thaddeus of Tver's.

attestations.note: The same man and the same day as the Greek, and the two agree on the age and the year. The Russian is the fuller of the two on the court he left: he was at the court of the empress Irene — whose reign it dates 797 to 802 — and of her son Constantine, refused all titles and honours to be tonsured, and at the emperor's own request stayed in a monastery of the capital rather than going out to the desert. Under the iconoclast Theophilus he was driven out of it by the heretics for rebuking the heresy, and wandered the country a long while.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Οκτωβρίου — «Όσιος Νικήτας ο Ομολογητής και Πατρίκιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους» and «Οσιος Νικητας ο Ομολογητης Και Πατρικιος (763 - 838)», and both years are repeated in the life — born 763, died at the age of 75 in 838 — so a `dates` object carries them. The office is the life's own: «ανέβηκε με την αρετή και την ικανότητά του στο αξίωμα του πατρικίου και στρατηγού της Σικελίας». **The «Στρατηγός του Βυζαντίου του 7ου μ.Χ. αιώνα» line above the life is saint.gr's note on the name Nicetas and not a statement about this saint** — a seventh-century general of Byzantium — and it is a near-miss with his real office, so it is named here to be sure it was not the source of it. The page's own uncertainty about his kinswoman is kept in the life in its own words: «η συγγένισσά του βασίλισσα Ειρήνη (άλλοι αναφέρουν Θεοδώρα)». The corpus keeps sixteen other men called Nicetas — of Pythia, of Medikion, of Chalcedon, the Goth, the Chartularius and the rest — and none of them is a patrician and general of Sicily or stands on this day. `locations` is left out: the page names Paphlagonia and Sicily but places him in neither for long. No hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).

birth.note: saint.gr: «καταγόταν από την Παφλαγονία και γεννήθηκε το έτος 763 μ.Χ.»

death.note: saint.gr: «σε ηλικία 75 χρονών απεβίωσε ειρηνικά το έτος 838 μ.Χ.», and its page head gives him as «(763 - 838)». days.pravoslavie.ru agrees on both figures and is less certain of the year: «Скончался он в возрасте 75 лет около 838 года», about 838, at the age of seventy-five. The bound is left at the year saint.gr states.
